The proof section — front and back

A — pairs, side by side

The two screenshots next to each other, labelled. No cleverness: what the customer sees, and what the staff run. Reads without being operated, works in a screenshot, and stacks cleanly on a phone.

Risk: it is the tallest of the three — two images per project means the section grows fast, and three pairs is already most of a screen. It also makes every project look equally strong, when only Horse & Harmony is genuinely one system.

B — the flip

One frame per project with a Front / Back toggle. Half the height of A, and the act of flipping is the argument — you are shown the same project twice and have to notice it is the same project.

Risk: a visitor who never clicks sees only half of it, and most visitors never click. It also cannot be screenshotted as proof, which matters for a page people send to a colleague.

C — overlap

The public site with the back office breaking out from behind it, one composite per project. The most designed of the three, and the only one where a single glance carries "these are the same thing".

Risk: the back office is the smaller image, and it is the harder thing to build — the composition puts the weaker claim forward. Also the fussiest to make work at 390px, where it becomes a stack anyway.
